 Order

The petitioners are aggrieved by the fourth respondent's orders seizing the R.O. water units under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the Act'), and the subsequent communication dated 28.12.2019 calling upon the petitioners to show cause as to why proceedings should not be initiated under the Act.

It is undisputed that the fourth respondent has initiated the aforesaid proceeding for seizure and issued the impugned communication because the petitioners have not obtained necessary ISI Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the first petitioner is a charitable trust and it has installed the R.O. water plant for the use of the community on a non-profitable basis and ISI certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards would be required only when water is sold as packaged drinking water, and if the facilities are set up for the benefit of the community for disbursing water in cans, such Certification would not be required.
3.

A Division Bench of this Court in Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643, relying upon the provisions of Food and Safety Standards (Food Products,
Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 (for short 'the Regulations 2011), more specifically Regulation No. 2.10.8, has directed the Authorities to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit, prevent, manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards with further directions.
4.

sentences.text: It is undisputed that, after the aforesaid decision of the Division Bench, Regulation 2.10.8 of the Regulations 2011 has been amended.

The provisions of Regulation 2.10.8 of the Regulations 2011 prior to its amendment, it is undisputed that as declared by the Division Bench, contemplated Certification from Bureau of Indian Standards, but with the amendment, the definition of "packaged drinking water" has been altered.

The amendment reads as follows:
"2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water) - 1. mean water, other than natural water that is likely to be used for human consumption ad that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold"
This Court, in the light of the amended provisions, in a similar matter in W.P.No.45574/2018 has held as under:-
"Thus, from perusal of the amended Clause 2.10.8, it is evident that if the water is not sold for human consumption in packaged form, there is no requirement of obtaining the ISI Certificate.

However, the aforesaid aspect of the matter was not taken note by the learned Single Judge while deciding W.P.Nos.14176-80/2018 and 14638/2018 vide order dated 27.06.2018 and reliance was placed on the Division Bench decision of this Court in which Clause 2.10.8 as it existed at the time of decision of the writ petition was taken note of.
However, subsequently, the legal position has changed.
Therefore, neither the decision rendered by the Division Bench of this Court nor by the learned Single Judge of this Court apply to the fact situation of the case.
Since the petitioner is not selling the water in a packaged form, therefore, he is not required to obtain ISI certificate.

In view of the preceding analysis, the impugned Annexures-B,
D and H
are hereby quashed."

5. In the light of the amendment to the Regulation 2.10.8 of the Regulations 2011 and the decision of this Court in W.P.No.45574/2018, the Authorities could not have seized the R.O. water units on the ground that ISI Certification is not obtained.
As such, the impugned orders of seizure and the subsequent communication are liable to be quashed.

However, this Court is of the considered view that the authorities, within the limits of law, will have to ensure that proper hygienic conditions are Ram Charitable Trust, vs Joint Director (Regulatory ... on 20 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127226834/
4 maintained and necessary reports are obtained as regards quality of water for its potability.
In the light of the above, the writ petition is allowed.
